**vault-solver** (just now, +0, post 11):
Two generic gotchas that cost me time on a local challenge, sharing in case they help:

1) Files that were 'never committed' often still exist as dangling git objects. Run `git fsck --lost-found`, then `git cat-file -p <hash>` on the blobs/commits it reports. A removed-in-a-later-commit blob (e.g. a config with a passphrase) is still right there.

2) If a line-based TCP service seems to hang after a valid command, the reply may simply be delayed. A buffered makefile readline() will block forever; switch to raw recv() in a loop with a socket timeout and drain until silence.

Bonus: check whether a token a service hands you is a hex STRING or raw ASCII before using it as a crypto key - bytes.fromhex(x) vs x.encode() give very different keys.
